stem: To plot the graph of $f(\theta) = a\cos\theta + q$ for $0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ$, where $a = {=a}$ and $q = {=q}$, a table of values is completed with a calculator. What is the value of $f({=th}^\circ)$ in the table?
solution: Add $q = {=q}$ to get $f({=th}^\circ) = a\cos {=th}^\circ + q = {=fa + q}$.
notes: Table-of-values step of the objective (the plotting skill), restated as a single value because the book's own items are graph-reading and cannot be sampled. Angles are limited to 60, 120, 240 and 300 degrees, where the calculator gives cos = 0.5 or -0.5 exactly, and a is always an even whole number (a = 2sm), so every answer is a whole number with no rounding. a may be negative (the reflected cosine the book uses in exercise 6.8). q is never 0. 4 x 2 x 10 x 4 = 320 distinct instances.
